title: Endowment Effect
description: We assign more value to things simply because we own them, even if we acquired them moments ago and for free.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: We assign more value to things simply because we own them, even if we acquired them moments ago and for free.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: Selling a used car: you list it for $5,000 because it’s yours and has memories, while buyers see a $3,500 vehicle.
A mug experiment: people given a mug demand twice as much to sell it as those who don’t own it are willing to pay.
You keep clothes you never wear because parting with them feels like losing value.

sections.title: Common Behaviors
content: Inflated asking prices for personal items.
Reluctance to trade items of equal market value.

sections.title: Real Phrases
content: “I can’t let it go for that little.”

sections.title: Warning Signs
content: You’re emotionally attached to an object’s price tag because it’s yours.
You expect buyers to care about your personal history with the item.
You refuse a fair offer simply because parting hurts.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: Loss aversion makes giving something up feel like a loss. Ownership integrates the item into the self-concept (Thaler, 1980; Kahneman, Knetsch, & Thaler, 1990). Once it’s “mine,” it’s special.

sections.title: Protection Strategy
content: Before selling or trading, ask: “What would I pay for this if I didn’t own it?”
Get an objective third-party valuation for high-value items.
Recognize that the sentimental premium only exists in your head.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
content: Assuming others will pay more because you value it more.
Letting the endowment effect block beneficial upgrades or decluttering.

sections.title: Real Scenario
sections.content: A designer upgrades her laptop. She tries to sell the old one for $800, citing “it’s still great.” Market price is $500. She insists for weeks, eventually selling for $520 after missing better offers. The delay cost her time and a faster sale.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Ownership is a lens that magnifies value in your eyes but not in the buyer’s. Take the lens off before pricing.
